steps.instruction: On the local desktop, confirm that the blue BASELINE window and magenta PRIVATE window are both readable over the synthetic test card.
Use Windows Snipping Tool or Print Screen on the fixture display. Inspect only the local preview, then delete the image without saving or uploading it.
In OBS, preview a Display Capture of the fixture display. Do not stream or retain a recording.
In a synthetic Zoom test meeting, share the fixture display and inspect the recipient view. Do not use a work meeting or real participant data.
In a synthetic Google Meet test room, share the fixture display from the supported browser and inspect the recipient view.
In a synthetic Microsoft Teams test meeting, share the fixture display and inspect the recipient view.
In a synthetic Webex test meeting, share the fixture display and inspect the recipient view.
Move focus among the capture client, test card, baseline window, and private window. Confirm that all remain reachable and that the fixture never takes focus back by itself.
With the fixture on the primary monitor at its normal scale, inspect a full-display capture preview.

Move all three fixture windows to a second monitor with a different scale or DPI, then inspect a full-display capture preview. If this hardware is unavailable, record not-run; the gate remains incomplete.
Place synthetic content in full-screen presentation mode while the two fixture windows remain locally visible, then inspect the shared-display preview.
While a local capture preview is active, sleep and resume Windows. Confirm both fixture windows return locally, then inspect the restarted capture preview.
Leave a capture preview open. The harness will terminate its fixture process. Confirm both synthetic windows disappear and the capture client remains under operator control.
Delete every screenshot, local recording, cloud recording, and test-room artifact created during this run. Keep only the content-free JSON manifest in the OS temporary directory.
